newsitem.title: CONGO: Rwandan refugees arrive in Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan refugees arrive in Brazzaville.

text.p: A convoy of barges chartered by the Congolese government arrived in Brazzaville on Thursday with more than 4,000 mostly Rwandan refugees on board.

Officials said the refugees would be transferred by truck to a camp at Bilolo, a former military training ground some 20 km (12 miles) north of the capital that was last used to house Tutsi refugees who fled Kinshasa in November of last year.
The majority of the refugees left North Kivu province in the east of what was then Zaire where they were housed in Mugunga camp near Goma until the end of 1996.

They then headed west ahead of the advance of Kabila's troops, going through Walikale, Tingi-Tingi camp, Kisangani, Bumba and Lisala on the Zaire river before crossing into Congo from the town of Mbandaka in what is now the Democratic Republic of Congo.
There were some young women and small children in the group, but close to 90 percent were men, mostly young men.
Laurent Kabila's war to topple Zaire's dictator Mobutu Sese Seko started as a revolt by ethnic Tutsis over citizenship. Tutsis were quickly hounded out of Kinshasa.

The refugees crossing this time are mostly Rwandan Hutus, among them former soldiers and hardliners accused of massacring up to 800,000 minority Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994 before fleeing to Zaire. They now fear revenge both from Kabila's Tutsi-led forces and the Tutsi-dominated army back in their homeland.
The convoy of six barges brought back refugees from sites as far north as Ndjoundou, some 400 km upriver from Brazzaville.
Chartered by the Congolese authorities, it was staffed by aid workers and accompanied by more than 50 Congolese troops.

After 12 days with the convoy the troops started to lose patience on Thursday and started firing into the air when the convoy was delayed some 30 km upriver from the capital while the authorities debated where the refugees should disembark.
The Congolese authorities are edgy about the refugees' presence in Congo and initially opposed designating them as "refugees", preferring the term "displaced persons in transit".
The government on Wednesday warned the refugees against behaving in a way likely to antagonise Kabila.
The massive presence of refugees on Congolese soil is unlikely to go down well with Kabila, whose spokesmen have warned neighbouring states against admitting armed Hutus.
Congolese Foreign Minister Destin-Arsene Tsaty-Mboungou said earlier this week that the government wanted the refugees to be repatriated as soon as possible.

"The United Nations High Commission for Refugees has agreed to finance the escorts and the means of transportation," said Alphonse Malanda, Senior Emergency Officer with UNHCR. "The government has to allocate us some troops."

Military sources said the Congolese authorities feared some of the refugees were so keen to avoid being sent back to Rwanda that they would try to leave Bilolo camp and head towards the Cameroon border, 800 km to the north.
